Predict on a raster grid

Source: R/predict.R
bruce_predict.Rd

Predicts the variable at the reference-network scale (no network offset, no station effect) for each day of the fitted window.

Usage

bruce_predict(
  fit,
  grid = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  dates = NULL,
  n_samples = 0,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95),
  keep_samples = FALSE,
  cap = TRUE,
  resample = "average",
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

fit

A bruce_fit.

grid

A terra::SpatRaster defining the prediction grid. Cells where its first layer is NA are skipped, so a masked raster works as a domain. NULL uses the covariate rasters' own grid.

domain

Optional polygon (sf or SpatVector) to mask the grid.

dates

Subset of the fitted days; NULL predicts all.

n_samples

Number of joint posterior samples. 0 returns posterior means only (fast, from INLA's marginal summaries). > 0 returns mean, standard deviation and quantiles from samples; requires the fit to have been made with keep_config = TRUE.

probs

Quantiles to return when sampling.

keep_samples

Keep the per-cell samples (needed by bruce_zonal() for uncertainty of zonal means). Memory grows as cells x samples x days.

cap

Cap covariates to the range observed at stations and background cells (avoids extrapolating linear effects).

resample

How each covariate is brought to the grid: "average" (block mean of the native raster over each grid cell, via terra::project()), "bilinear", or "near" (the native raster's value at the grid cell centre, read directly from that raster in its own projection). A single value or a named vector, e.g. c(elev = "average", svf = "near"). Rasters that already share the grid's geometry are used as they are.

seed

Seed for posterior sampling. A number makes samples reproducible (INLA then samples on one thread); NULL samples in parallel, faster but not reproducible.

Value

An object of class bruce_prediction with mean, sd and quantiles (SpatRasters with one layer per day) and, optionally, samples.
